correctness.rationale: All operator norms reduce exactly to continuous scalar maximizations. The leading comparison at t=pi/n and radial positivity localize every maximizer at nt->pi. A coercive u^2/4 phase penalty yields u=O(epsilon), and a uniform second-order expansion plus a complete square gives the two coefficients and phase drift. On t=x n^{-1/alpha}, uniform local convergence plus exponentially small tails proves the exact power-difference constant. The numerical checker supports finite examples only, not infinite claims.

value.rationale: The norm-two saturation boundary and Ritt obstruction are motivated directly by the recent initiating spectral-tangency example. The exact first and second norm-gap coefficients reveal the phase-versus-radial competition, distinguish the second radial spectral jet from a universal optimizer correction, and give a measurable dynamical growth coefficient for the same tangency exponent. General rate-only results do not supply these precise invariants; the parameter family and low smoothness make it a natural stability law rather than an arbitrary finite computation.
